Trump suspend les frappes américaines contre l’Iran AFP. D ans un message sur sa plateforme Truth Social, Donald Trump a affirmé dimanche que les Etats-Unis sont « prêts à frapper la République islamique d’Iran, à des niveaux de terreur militaire, de force et de puissance jamais vus depuis la Seconde Guerre mondiale ». « Malgré cela, nous venons d’être priés par l’Iran, et par d’autres pays du Moyen-Orient, de suspendre toute attaque », a-t-il indiqué. « Sur la base de cette demande, j’ai accepté… d’annuler l’attaque, sous réserve de pouvoir conclure rapidement un ACCORD. Israël se joint à moi dans cet engagement », a-t-il dit. Cette annonce intervient peu après que les Etats-Unis ont appelé leurs ressortissants à « envisager de quitter » le Moyen-Orient en raison d’une possible « escalade » du conflit régional. a noter que vendredi, Donald Trump avait menacé lors d’un conseil des ministres de frapper l’Iran « très fort ». Selon des médias américains, Washington envisageait de nouveaux bombardements massifs au cours du week-end. D’après CBS News, les Etats-Unis et Israël préparaient des frappes conjointes, visant les raffineries de pétrole et les centrales électriques comptant parmi les cibles possibles. Dans son message dimanche, le président américain a déclaré que l’accord avec l’Iran devrait inclure l’ouverture « COMPLÈTE ET TOTALE DU DÉTROIT D’ORMUZ, ainsi qu’une fin de la menace nucléaire iranienne ». Le prince héritier saoudien Mohammed Ben Salmane a appelé Donald Trump samedi pour exprimer ses inquiétudes concernant ses projets de frappes, a rapporté Axios, citant des responsables américains anonymes. « Désamorcer » Une source au fait de l’appel a indiqué à Axios que le prince héritier saoudien avait « exhorté Trump à désamorcer la situation et à s’abstenir de lancer les frappes ». La Maison-Blanche n’a pas immédiatement répondu à une demande de commentaire concernant cette information de presse. Jeudi, le Pakistan, pays médiateur, avait affirmé que les belligérants négociaient en vue d’une désescalade, en particulier concernant le détroit d’Ormuz, passage stratégique au cœur des tensions et verrouillé par Téhéran. Mais l’armée iranienne avait accusé samedi les Etats-Unis de favoriser l’« escalade des tensions » dans la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Mercredi, un drone a frappé un navire gazier appartenant à une société américaine, amarré dans un port égyptien. L’Egypte mène une enquête mais n’a, à ce stade, accusé aucun groupe d’être à l’origine de l’attaque. À lire aussi Les quatre pierres d’achoppement qui compromettent la paix entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis Dans une interview publiée sur Fox News avant l’annonce de Donald Trump, son secrétaire d’Etat Marco Rubio assure que les capacités militaires de l’Iran ont été amoindries et que les responsables iraniens « sont maintenant disposés, et dans certains cas semblent impatients, à conclure un accord sur la dénucléarisation ». La guerre au Moyen-Orient a été déclenchée le 28 février par des frappes conjointes des Etats-Unis et d’Israël contre l’Iran, qui a riposté par des attaques de missiles et de drones dans la région. Malgré un protocole d’accord signé à la mi-juin pour ouvrir la voie à des pourparlers de paix, de nouvelles frappes réciproques ont eu lieu début juillet. La guerre s’est étendue récemment avec un nouveau front en mer Rouge, où les rebelles yéménites Houthis, soutenus par l’Iran, ont annoncé imposer un blocus aux ports saoudiens et ont depuis revendiqué des attaques contre des pétroliers et des installations pétrolières du royaume. Ces mesures font peser une menace sur la circulation maritime par le détroit stratégique de Bab el-Mandeb, à la limite sud de la mer Rouge, dont l’importance s’est accrue depuis le blocage du détroit d’Ormuz. Les rebelles ont cependant démenti samedi vouloir imposer des droits de passage aux navires franchissant le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, comme allégué par un ministre yéménite. Le regain de tension au Moyen-Orient avait provoqué cette semaine une nouvelle hausse des prix du pétrole, avec notamment une flambée de 7,66 % du baril de Brent (à 90,53 dollars) mercredi. Le président Donald Trump a déclaré samedi que les Etats-Unis et Israël avaient convenu de suspendre les nouvelles frappes prévues contre l’Iran à la demande de Téhéran et d’autres pays de la région, à condition qu’un accord soit rapidement conclu. Si la spéciale a été interrompue, les deux hommes ont toutefois réussi à sortir sans assistance de leur véhicule, a communiqué l’équipe Toyota dans la foulée. « Ils sont tous les deux conscients et OK dans l’ensemble, et ils vont être transportés à l’hôpital pour subir des examens complémentaires. » Ogier a été transporté en hélicoptère et Ingrassia en ambulance a précisé la FIA. Dans la soirée, l’équipe Toyota a donné des nouvelles rassurantes des deux Français. « Les résultats des examens à l’hôpital de Seb et Julien ont été positifs », a-t-elle communiqué sur les réseaux sociaux. « En raison de la violence du choc lors de l’accident, ils resteront en observation pendant la nuit à l’hôpital ». Sébastien Ogier a posté un message rassurant samedi : : « Julien et moi sommes tous les deux allés à l’hôpital pour des examens et nous y passerons la nuit par précaution après ce violent impact. Mais nous nous sentons tous les deux bien, c’est le plus important. (…) L’essentiel est que nous soyons entiers. » Voir cette publication sur Instagram Une publication partagée par Sébastien Ogier (@sebogier) Et d’ajouter : « Un grand merci à l’équipe d’avoir construit une voiture aussi solide. Sébastien Ogier et son copilote Julien Ingrassia ont été hospitalisés après leur violente sortie de retour samedi au Rallye de Finlande. Mais Sébastien Ogier s’est montré rassurant. Quetta coal mine explosion: Search and rescue operation concludes as last two bodies recovered. QUETTA: The bodies of the remaining two miners trapped following a methane gas explosion in a mine near Quetta were found on Saturday. The explosion occurred on Thursday at a private coal mine in the Sorange coalfield, about 30 kilometres northeast of Quetta. The methane gas explosion triggered a fire, caused the mine to collapse, and affected another nearby mine. Balochistan Chief Inspector of Mines Muhammad Atif confirmed to Dawn that “all 34 bodies of coal miners trapped” in the mines have been recovered. He added that the last two bodies were recovered after hectic search efforts. The bodies of 32 miners were recovered on Friday. Atif said both mines were sealed after the rescue operation was completed and a probe into the tragic incident has been ordered. “A team of mining experts has been formed, which has initiated a probe into the incident,” the official said. All of the miners hailed from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Shangla district, Atif said, adding that their bodies have been dispatched to their native villages. “Twenty-three miners who lost their lives belonged to Pirabad alone,” he added. Abid Yaar, president of the Shangla Coal Mine Workers Association, said on Friday that Mian Kalay in Pir Abad — from where at least 23 of the miners hailed — had become an epicentre of repeated coal mine tragedies. He added that the victims, aged between 17 and 25, belonged to the same families and were cousins or close relatives. According to Yaar, several of the deceased were orphans whose fathers had also lost their lives in previous coal mine accidents. Out of the 34 miners, 24 were working about 4,000 feet underground in the first mine where the methane gas explosion occurred, while the rest were working in another nearby mine. Deadly mine explosions are common in Balochistan, with stakeholders often pointing out the absence of essential safety protocols. Coal mining has historically been fraught with hazards, which are similar to those associated with the aftermath of natural disasters: suffocation, gas poisoning, roof collapse, rock burst, gas explosions and a plethora of lung diseases, including incurable diseases like coalworker’s pneumoconiosis, also known as black lung disease.

Parts of Karachi receive light showers; more rain expected. KARACHI: Parts of Karachi received light rain on Saturday, with the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) predicting more showers till Monday. Light rain was reported in Gulshan-i-Maymar, Gulshan-i-Hadeed, Super Highway and nearby areas, DawnNewsTV reported. Meanwhile, the PMD has predicted light to moderate rain with dust and thunderstorm in Karachi from today till August 3. According to the forecast, a westerly wave, affecting the northern areas, is likely to strengthen and affect upper and central parts of the country. Under the influence of the system, moderate rainfall with dust and thunderstorms is likely in Karachi from Saturday (today) till Monday with occasional gaps, it said. It also forecast moderate to heavy rainfall in Tharparkar, Umerkot, Mirpurkhas, Badin, Sanghar, Khairpur, Tando Muhammad Khan, Tando Allahyar, Hyderabad, Matiari and Shaheed Benazirabad districts. The department also forecast rainfall with dust and thunderstorm in Ghotki, Kashmore, Jacobabad, Shikarpur, Sukkur, Qambar Shahdadkot, Larkana, Naushahro Feroze, Thatta and Jamshoro districts. For Saturday, the department said that the maximum temperature was expected to range between 34 and 36 degrees Celsius in the port city. It predicted cloudy weather with a chance of rain accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds.

Tourists barred from visiting Saiful Muluk. MANSEHRA: The dist­rict administration on Fri­­day barred tourists from travelling to Lake Saiful Muluk after the Pakistan Meteorological Depart­m­ent (PMD) forecast more monsoon rain and possible cloudbursts in Naran, the commercial hub of Kaghan Valley. “The district administration has imposed the ban at the request of the NDMA and the PDMA to ensure the safety of tourists, as heavy rains and possible cloudbursts are expected in the coming days,” Balakot As­­sistant Commissioner Has­­rat Khan told reporters. An order issued by the district administration stat­­ed that, in light of the PMD’s forecast of heavy rainfall and possible cloudbursts, all travel to Lake Saiful Muluk would remain banned until further orders. Meanwhile, the business community in Kaghan Valley urged the district administration to reconsider its decision to suspend travel to the popular tourist destination. “The district administration has already placed all its departments and Rescue 1122 on high alert in Kaghan Valley. In such a situation, travel to Lake Saiful Muluk is not dangerous,” Hussan Deen, chai­­rman of a traders’ body in Kaghan Valley, said. He said the weather in the valley, particularly in Naran, remained pleasant and tourists should continue to visit the area. “Our business activities are limited to only three to four months each year. Such restrictions on travel to tourist attractions discourage visitors and adve­rsely affect our busines­ses,” Mr Deen said. Published in Dawn, August 1st, 2026

CDF Munir says Pak-China friendship has remained steadfast amid evolving regional, global challenges. Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir said on Saturday that the friendship between Pakistan and China is “unique, time-tested and has remained steadfast in the face of evolving regional and global challenges”. He made the remarks while addressing a gathering at the General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi, held to commemorate the 99th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Liberation Army (PLA), Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. It said that China’s Ambassador to Pakistan Jiang Zaidong was the guest of honour on the occasion. China’s Defence Attaché Major General Wang Zhong, officials from the Chinese Embassy and senior military officers from Pakistan’s tri-services also attended the ceremony. According to ISPR, Field Marshal Munir extended a warm welcome to the distinguished guests and congratulated the PLA on the occasion of its 99th founding anniversary. “He paid tribute to the PLA’s remarkable contributions to China’s defence, national development and international peace and security,” it said. “Highlighting the enduring strength of Pakistan-China relations, the field marshal observed that friendship between the two countries is unique, time-tested and has remained steadfast in the face of evolving regional and global challenges,” it said. “He reaffirmed that Pakistan armed forces and the PLA are true partners, bound by mutual trust, unwavering support and a shared commitment to regional peace, stability and the protection of common strategic interests,” the statement said. It added that the Chinese ambassador expressed sincere appreciation to the field marshal for hosting the commemorative event. “He acknowledged the Pakistan armed forces’ significant contributions and sacrifices in the fight against terrorism and reaffirmed China’s unwavering support for Pakistan and its enduring commitment to further strengthening the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries,” the statement concluded. At last year’s commemoration ceremony at GHQ, COAS Munir had stressed that the “enduring partnership” between Pakistan and China will continue to play a pivotal role in regional stability. Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and regional connectivity. Over the decades, ties have expanded across different sectors — including trade, energy, defence and infrastructure — with the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) symbolising a shared vision for development. Both neighbours maintain close cooperation in various fields, with companies from both countries signing agreements worth $850 million at a pharmaceutical conference last month. A day before that, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with a delegation of China’s National Immigration Administration. The two sides agreed to enhance cooperation in immigration, border management and institutional collaboration. That development came within two weeks of Naqvi meeting his Chinese counterpart Ling Zhifeng in New York, where the interior minister had gone to attend a United Nations summit.

Cleric affiliated with JUI-F shot dead in Lower South Waziristan. LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: A cleric affiliated with the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), Maulana Muhammad Ismail, was shot dead by unidentified armed men in the Azam Warsak area of Birmal tehsil in Lower South Waziristan, it emerged on Saturday. District Police Officer (DPO) Muhammad Tahir said that the incident occurred after Friday prayers when unidentified assailants on a motorcycle opened fire on Ismail, killing him on the spot. The official said the assailants managed to escape from the scene. The DPO said that an initial report of the incident had been registered and an investigation into the killing had been launched. He added that police were examining the incident from all angles. According to police officials and local tribal elders, the deceased was a resident of Kazha Panga and was serving as a teacher at a religious seminary in the area. In May, renowned cleric and former JUI-F MPA Maulana Muhammad Idrees was killed in Charsadda after unidentified assailants opened fire on him. In January, JUI-F leader Maulana Sultan Muhammad Wazir succumbed to his injuries after being critically wounded in a bomb blast near a madressah in South Waziristan’s Wana bazaar area.

Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, others perish in Broad Peak avalanche, climbing company confirms. Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja died along with other team members in a powerful avalanche on Broad Peak, his climbing company confirmed on Saturday. The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off contact with the international expedition led by 43-year-old British-Nepali climber Purja. “It is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal Purja tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak,” Purja’s company Elite Expeditions said on social media. “We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive,” it added. The remains recovered so far — flown by helicopter to hospital for formal identification — included an American woman, an Omani woman and a Nepali man, the Gilgit-Baltistan government said in a statement released on Friday night. Purja, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, broke multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide. Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah offered his condolences over the “tragic” deaths of Purja and the other climbers, which he said “has shocked us”. “The physical journey of all the deceased climbers… has been interrupted, but the history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring,” Shah said in a statement on social media. Police in GB said in a statement that high-altitude porters and rescue teams were carrying out a second day of the operation on Saturday after the search was paused due to difficult weather conditions a day earlier. Rescuers and army helicopters had been scouring the area and teams stayed at the base camp overnight, according to the GB government. “The rescue operation is being conducted under extremely challenging terrain and high-altitude weather conditions by the Pakistani army in coordination with local high-altitude climbers and rescuers,” it said. Powerful avalanche The avalanche struck while the mountaineers were on a mission to summit Broad Peak (8,047 metres, or 26,400 feet) on Thursday and while the team was ascending at an altitude of around 6,600 metres, according to regional authorities. The expedition comprised 10 people — including Purja, five Nepalis, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, and a climber from China. The team was last in contact on Thursday morning, the official statement said, with reports emerging that evening of the powerful avalanche. “Data from their tracking devices indicates that they were thrown hundreds of metres down the mountainside,” Naila Kiani, from Pakistan’s Alpine Club, told Le Monde newspaper. Fida Ali, a climber in the area who worked closely with Purja since 2023, told AFP their focus for the climbing season was summiting Broad Peak, but they had first tackled another mountain, G2, in harsh weather. Ali also joined the expedition to Broad Peak in its initial stages but returned early to accompany a Russian climber who was feeling the effects of exhaustion — narrowly avoiding the fatal avalanche. “I wanted to go with him (Purja) but couldn’t and came back with her. I was part of the team but survived,” he told AFP . Super peaks Purja had written on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 “super peaks” twice without oxygen. “Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down,” he wrote. He had climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders” (peaks above 8,000 metres) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 — then a record. Broad Peak is the world’s 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre-plus ascents. It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.

PML-N, PPP leaders resume talks to ease tensions over AJK polls. MUZAFFARABAD: Senior leaders of the PML-N and PPP on Saturday resumed talks aimed at defusing tensions between the two parties following the latter’s allegations of rigging in four of the 13 constituencies in Mirpur division during the first phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections. The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged in the lead during the first phase of polls. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. The latest round of talks followed two earlier meetings — the first at a local hotel on Thursday night and the second before noon on Friday. The PML-N delegation comprised Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah, Federal Minister for Kashmir Affairs Amir Muqam, and PML-N AJK chapter secretary general and MLA-elect Chaudhry Tariq Farooq. Representing the PPP were former Senate chairman Nayyar Bokhari, former federal minister Qamar Zaman Kaira and AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who also serves as secretary general of the party’s AJK chapter. PPP leader Nadeem Afzal Chan attended the Friday meeting but was absent from today’s session. The meetings reviewed security arrangements ahead of the second phase of polling on Sunday. Both sides agreed that the Election Commission, as well as the divisional and district administrations, should leave no room for lapses in ensuring extraordinary security measures so that voters could exercise their franchise freely. According to sources, the discussions also focused on the PPP’s allegations of rigging and its subsequent demand for repolling in certain constituencies. The PPP was told that neither the government nor any institution had facilitated or backed rigging and that, if irregularities had occurred at any polling station, they were localised incidents rather than the result of any organised plan. “It was not planned or pre-planned rigging but isolated acts at places where supporters of one candidate enjoyed numerical dominance over their opponents. Such incidents have unfortunately been part of the territory’s polling atmosphere and have also been witnessed in previous elections,” a source quoted the PML-N leaders as telling their counterparts. The PML-N leadership maintained that, unlike the PPP, it had begun election preparations well in advance and had enforced greater organisational discipline through constituency-level planning. The PPP, they claimed, had remained under the impression that the elections would be delayed by a year and that the 12 refugee constituencies would be abolished, which prevented it from focusing on electoral preparations in time. The meeting also discussed ways to address the complaints through both political dialogue and legal channels, the source said. According to the sources, the PPP had initially raised objections to the results in four constituencies: Charhoi, Sehnsa and Nakyal in Kotli district, and Barnala in Bhimber district. However, it later withdrew its allegations regarding Sehnsa and Barnala. Saturday’s discussions centred on Charhoi, where PPP AJK president Chaudhry Yasin lost to the PML-N’s Raja Riasat, and Nakyal, where PPP candidate Javed Iqbal Budhanvi was defeated by the PML-N’s Raja Ayaz Ahmed. The sources said the PML-N had presented a detailed analysis of the results, showing that while its candidates had secured more than 80 per cent of the votes at some polling stations, the PPP had also won more than 80pc of the votes at others. “If any irregularities occurred, they occurred on both sides, and a mechanism has been discussed to address them, legally and politically,” said a PML-N leader. The meeting tasked both regional secretary generals — Rathore and Farooq — with contacting the Election Commission to explore a legal resolution to the dispute. Another meeting had been scheduled for Saturday afternoon, but it could not be held because Sanaullah and Muqam had to leave for Islamabad owing to urgent engagements. Both parties traded barbs earlier this week after the conclusion of the first phase of elections in AJK, with the PPP chairman alleging rigging in the polls and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz urging the PPP to accept defeat. The PML-N grabbed nine out of the 13 constituencies of AJK’s Mirpur division in the elections. In a televised statement, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz hailed the “ outstanding victory ” of the PML-N in the first phase of the AJK elections, urging the PPP to accept defeat. “The PPP should have accepted its defeat by affirming the spirit of democracy, but I felt aggrieved by the kind of words used by PPP leaders.” “The state does not decide election results; only the people make this decision,” she said in response to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations. On Thursday, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari warned that a stolen election in AJK would start a “ countdown ” for the federal government. “If you steal [the election] … write it down, take my guarantee, that a countdown will start for your federal government,” he warned. “If you steal my mandate, I will come for your throne.”

Bilawal receives JAAC response on reconciliation commission, says AJK PM to consult stakeholders on way forward. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Saturday said he had received a response from the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) to his letter proposing the establishment of a Truth and Reconciliation Commission, adding that the party would now consult key stakeholders to determine the way forward. The PPP has repeatedly called for the establishment of a truth and reconciliation commission amid protests in AJK. Over the past month, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues — most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly reserved for refugees from Indian-occupied Jammu and Kashmir who settled in mainland Pakistan after 1947, which has resulted in protests across the region. In a post on X, Bilawal welcomed the group’s “willingness to engage with the proposed commission” as a possible institutional mechanism to address the crisis, noting that the proposal had also been endorsed by the Azad Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly. The PPP chairman maintained that his “foremost priority” is to help bring an end to the “ongoing crisis” and provide relief to the region’s people and restore normal life in AJK as “soon as possible”. “The loss of every precious life is a national tragedy.” Bilawal said he would now consult AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who would seek initial input from the federal government and other relevant stakeholders to determine whether there was sufficient common ground to move forward with a mutually agreed proposal. Earlier, Bilawal said he had been campaigning for the formation of the commission for the past month. Addressing a public gathering of party workers in Muzaffarabad earlier this week, the PPP chairman said: “It is necessary that during these historic elections, we restore peace and maintain fairness and transparency. To honour the future of Kashmir and Pakistan’s stance on Kashmir, this is not about anyone’s victory or defeat. The state and the protesters will have to accept this recommendation from the PPP.” The region’s legislative assembly had also endorsed a resolution asking for the establishment of an independent reconciliation commission to investigate the violence and pave the way for a negotiated settlement. JAAC ban The regional government on June 5 declared the JAAC a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act. The notification by AJK’s Home Department said the group was “engaged in terrorism” and acted in a manner “prejudicial to peace and security” of the state. It further stated that JAAC was involved in “creating anarchy in the state by intimidating public, promoting hatred and creating a sense of insecurity in society and public at large etc”. Following the ban, local authorities launched a crackdown against the organisation, arresting scores of its leaders and activists from different areas. In a televised press conference on July 28, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar alleged the involvement of militant elements within JAAC, adding that they were pursuing a foreign agenda and backed by Indian funding. The information minister reiterated claims made earlier in the day by the region’s information secretary and a senior police official that a significant number of protesters participating in the proscribed JAAC demonstration in AJK were affiliated with Fitna Al Khawarij .

US to make visa bond programme permanent for people from dozens of countries. The US State Department will make permanent a visa bond programme that could require applicants from 50 countries, mostly from Africa, to post bonds of up to $20,000 when seeking US visas, according to a federal notice posted online on Friday. The Federal Register notice applies to B1 and B2 visas, which are issued for business and tourism travel. “Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers,” the notice said. “The 2025 visa bond pilot, which provided a framework for the Department of State, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Department of the Treasury to assess the feasibility of administering a visa bond programme, has provided sufficient data to suggest that a visa bond programme is an effective tool for enforcing compliance among bonded visa holders.” In the pilot programme, consular officers could require bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or up to $15,000. The final rule eliminates the $5,000 option and raises the maximum bond to $20,000. The final rule goes into effect on August 3 when it is scheduled for publication in the Federal Register. In the list of 50 countries for whose citizens this programme applies, 30 are from Africa. US officials say the policy is intended to reduce visa overstays. Immigration advocates argue it will deter legitimate travel to the United States. Rights advocates say President Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown violates free speech and due process, while creating an unsafe environment for ethnic minorities and encouraging racial profiling. Trump has defended the measures as necessary to bolster national security. While Trump says he wants to curb illegal immigration, his administration has made legal immigration more difficult, for example, by imposing new and expensive fees for applicants of certain visas and by enforcing social media vetting for applicants and immigrants already in the country. Earlier in May, the State Department identified nationals from the following 50 countries as being required to post visa bonds: Algeria, Angola, Antigua and Barbuda, Bangladesh, Benin, Bhutan, Botswana, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Central African Republic, Cote D’Ivoire, Cuba, Djibouti, Dominica, Ethiopia, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Georgia, Grenada, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kyrgyz Republic, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Mongolia, Mozambique, Namibia, Nepal, Nicaragua, Nigeria, Papua New Guinea, Sao Tome and Principe, Senegal, Seychelles, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tunisia, Turkmenistan, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu, Venezuela, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

Army major martyred in North Waziristan IBO: ISPR. An army officer was martyred during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Razmak area of North Waziristan district, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement on Saturday. During the operation, security forces also killed five terrorists affiliated with Fitna al Khawarij , according to the military’s media wing. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). The ISPR said that Major Hafiz Ihsan Elahi, 34, from Mianwali district, was “a brave officer who was leading his troops from the front, fought gallantly, paid the ultimate sacrifice” and embraced martyrdom. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed terrorists, “who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities” against security forces and law enforcement agencies, as well as in the killing of civilians. “Sanitisation operations are being conducted to eliminate any other India-sponsored terrorist found in the area. Relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision ‘ Azm-i-Istehkam ’ (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” the ISPR statement read. “Such sacrifices of our brave soldiers further reinforce our unwavering commitment of safeguarding our nation at all costs.” Earlier this week, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the government was implementing a comprehensive and effective strategy to “completely eliminate” the menace posed by the proscribed Fitna-al-Hindustan , Fitna-al-Khawarij and other terrorist outfits to the country. Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism since the banned TTP ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks. Last month, in the wake of multiple major attacks in Balochistan, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir had reaffirmed that terrorism “emanating from across the borders will be crushed with full might of the state”. On July 29, the military’s media wing said security forces killed 32 terrorists during operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. 7 terrorists killed in Nushki IBO In a separate statement , ISPR said security forces killed “seven Indian-sponsored terrorists” during an IBO in Balochistan’s Nushki district on the night of July 30/31 July. Among those was a would-be suicide bomber, the ISPR said, noting that the IBO was carried out on the “reported presence of terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan ” — a term designated by the state for terrorist organisations in Balo­chistan. During the operation, a terrorist hideout was “identified, monitored and busted through prompt surgical action by own forces, killing all seven Indian sponsored terrorists, including a suicide bomber”, the statement said. It added that ammunition and improvised explosive devices found there were also destroyed on-site. Sanitisation operations were underway to eliminate “any other Indian sponsored terrorist found in the area”. The military’s media affairs wing reaffirmed that the counter-terrorism campaign under Vision Azm-i-Istehkam would continue “at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and -supported terrorism from the country”. A day earlier, Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti vowed that the state would not retreat “even an inch” in its fight against terrorism. Last month, security forces killed at least 16 terrorists during “Operation Al-Azm” in Balochistan’s Mastung district, which was launched after a shooting on a Karachi-bound coach claimed three lives and injured five others. Security concerns heightened in Balochistan after a spate of major terrorist attacks took place in early July, which prompted counterterrorism operations across the province. Among the counterterrorism efforts was Operation Shaban , in which 91 terrorists were killed between July 5 and July 16, according to security sources cited by state media. This took the tally of terrorists eliminated in operations across the province during the period to 129.

July deadliest month of 2026 as 205 lives lost, 401 terrorists killed: PICSS. ISLAMABAD: Violence linked to terrorist attacks and counter-terrorism operations intensified sharply in July, making it the deadliest month of 2026, with 112 security personnel among 205 people killed, while 401 terrorists were eliminated. The Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based think tank, said in its monthly security assessment that fatalities among security personnel and terrorists rose substantially during the month as terrorist violence increased and security forces intensified counter-terrorism operations. According to the report, at least 112 security personnel lost their lives during July, the highest monthly toll since January 2023 and the second-highest recorded in more than a decade. In January 2023, 114 security personnel were martyred, including around 102 in the suicide bombing at Peshawar Police Lines, the report recalled. It said 401 terrorists were killed during July, the highest number recorded in a single month in more than a decade. On the other hand, 74 civilians and 19 members of peace committees lost their lives in July. The death toll among peace committee members was also the highest recorded in a single month during the past decade. According to PICSS, the 232 injuries during July included 101 security personnel, 103 civilians, 14 peace committee members and 14 terrorists. The data showed that, compared with June, security personnel deaths increased by 195pc, rising from 38 to 112. Terrorist deaths increased by 109pc, from 192 to 401, while civilian deaths rose by 21pc, from 61 to 74. The institute recorded at least eight suicide attacks during July, including five vehicle-borne suicide attacks. The think tank noted that this was the highest number of suicide attacks recorded in a single month during the past decade. Kidnapping incidents also doubled during the month, rising by 100pc from 33 in June to 66 in July. Province-wise breakdown It stated that the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan, where the overall death toll increased by 241pc, from 109 in June to 372 in July. Security personnel deaths in Balochistan increased from six in June to 62 in July, representing a rise of 933pc. Terrorist deaths rose from 75 to 238, while civilian deaths increased by 93pc, from 28 to 54. Eighteen members of peace committees were also killed in the province. According to the report, mainland Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, representing an increase of 105pc. The number of people injured rose from 60 to 98. Security personnel deaths in mainland KP increased from 12 to 38, while terrorist deaths rose by 192pc, from 37 to 108. Civilian deaths, however, declined by 73pc, falling from 26 in June to seven in July. One member of a peace committee was also killed in the province. Data showed a slight decline in overall deaths in the merged districts of KP, formerly known as Fata. The region recorded 79 deaths in July, compared with 85 in June. The number of people injured in the merged districts declined by 37pc, from 60 to 38. Security personnel deaths increased from six to 11, while terrorist deaths declined by 24pc, from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13. In Sindh, it recorded two terrorist attacks in which one security personnel member was killed. The province had recorded 12 deaths in June. Security forces also arrested six suspected terrorists during counter-terrorism operations in Sindh. Punjab, Islamabad, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan witnessed no terrorist violence during July. However, security forces arrested three suspected terrorists during operations conducted in Punjab. Overall, the data showed that the first seven months of 2026 witnessed 2,786 deaths linked to terrorist violence and counter-terrorism operations. Those killed included 1,857 terrorists, 463 civilians, 434 security forces personnel and 32 members of peace committees. The average martyrdoms per month among security forces increased from 56 in 2025 to 62 in 2026, while average deaths of civilians increased from 48 to 66, and average deaths among the terrorists increased from 178 to 265 per month.

‘Enough is enough’: MQM-P leaders, Shahid Khaqan back creation of new administrative units. Former premier Shahid Khaqan Abbasi and MQM-P leaders Dr Farooq Sattar and Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Saturday backed the creation of additional administrative units in the country. On Thursday, Naqvi urged all political parties to “settle” various national-level issues, including the question of creating new provinces . Addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 being held in Islamabad, Naqvi said there was “only one solution” to improving the country’s overall condition: “You will have to take [the matter of] administrative units, provinces or whatever you may call it, to the public.” Addressing a press conference in Karachi today, MQM leader Dr Farooq Sattar said that, due to immense population growth, additional administrative units were essential to ensure proper governance. “No country in the world has seen population growth as fast as ours,” he said. “We need to manage and administer that, but how will we do that without additional administrative units?” Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui and MQM Deputy Convener Dr Farooq Sattar address a press conference in Karachi on August 1, 2026. — Screengrab via YouTube/Dawn News Sattar noted that, with such a large population, questions arose about how administrations would be able to address fundamental issues and ensure effective service delivery. “Two things have become clear: we need administrative units. Enough is enough,” he declared. “The ad-hocism we have seen for around 80 years must end. [Interior Minister] Mohsin Naqvi presented a clear administrative framework for Pakistan’s future in his speech, which is welcomed by citizens from all walks of life.” “Pakistan’s economy is tied to its political and administrative structure.” “We need curative treatment, not symptomatic treatment,” he stated. Sattar added that the door needs to be left open for Gen-Z to play a representative role in Pakistan’s political, economic and social landscape. “Political parties should move in this direction, as they are of the opinion that the system is infertile; it cannot ensure people’s prosperity or progress, build national consensus or strength, or guarantee the country’s security,” he stated. “If we want to avail ourselves of these benefits, Pakistan must walk among the world with its head held high; the youth have to stand on their feet; we have to look the world and the IMF (International Monetary Fund) in the eye and talk to them. New administrative units are essential for this; without them, we will not move forward.” Speaking before Sattar, Education Minister Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui noted that the conference addressed by Naqvi was an economic one, not a political one. “We understand that there are no higher administrative units other than districts and divisions within a province. With One Unit, provinces were dissolved, but they returned after the end of the One Unit scheme in a different form,” he said, addressing the press conference. “This issue of the limits of administrative units never existed, nor was it part of Pakistan’s politics. Are these [units] so sacred that we cannot talk about them? When nobody spoke about them, we did,” Siddiqui added. He also stated that no matter which province people live in, they are still living within Pakistan, noting that the state itself is indivisible. “The Constitution demands the division of provinces. But because of the pressure from a growing population, the procedures outlined in 1973 can no longer be enforced. This is why the MQM submitted an amendment bill in the National Assembly; it was not opposed and has been supported by the standing committee,” Siddiqui said. “This MQM demand, which is in accordance with Pakistan’s population growth, is an administrative necessity and addresses the country’s economic issues,” he added. “Our voice is being echoed by others. Today, we thank you all for highlighting this need during the month of Pakistan’s independence.” Siddiqui said the party further believed that the current system of democracy, “where benefits never reach the people”, was not needed. Ex-PM Abbasi says system needs to be changed Former prime minister and Awaam Pakistan convener Shahid Khaqan Abbasi also addressed a press conference at the National Press Club in Islamabad, stating that the current state of affairs could not continue for much longer, but noted that the government was beginning to realise it. “I am grateful to my interior minister for acknowledging after four or five years that the country is not running,” he stated. “It should have been discussed in parliament or the cabinet. The country knows it is not running, but it has finally dawned on the rulers.” Abbasi added that the military’s spokesperson had acknowledged this during his press conference on Friday and that reform was the only way to keep the country functioning, but “there are always people who do not want meaningful change”. “This is a matter of interests; if we talk about reforms in this country, then those whose interests do not align with reforms will oppose them,” he added. “The country is not being run well; we do not have money, and we are not ready to undertake reforms. “Reforms are needed in this country; otherwise, the situation will get worse. Your debts, costs and taxes will continue to increase.” Abbasi noted that simply creating new provinces would not solve the issue, but that the entire system needed to be changed. “After 78 years, we don’t know how to buy flour. Our farmers have been ruined, and today we are even importing wheat by spending precious dollars,” he said, alleging that those in power were more interested in purchasing official vehicles and aircraft than addressing the hardships faced by ordinary citizens. He stressed that constitutional supremacy and the rule of law were necessary for political stability and economic growth. “Without the rule of law, investment will not come, and without investment there can be no sustainable economic progress,” Abbasi said. ‘Better late than never’ In a post on X, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif voiced his agreement with Naqvi on the matter of new provinces, but criticised the interior minister for failing to raise the issue earlier and for not implementing the 12 points of the National Action Plan that fall within his remit. “As a political worker, I also strongly feel that the system’s evolutionary process has, for decades, remained subject to group and personal interests. It needs to be freed from those influences,” he wrote. Asif also suggested that the matter be discussed in both parliament and the cabinet, adding that doing so would strengthen institutions and the system, while any changes would proceed through the constitutional process. “Mr Naqvi is a highly respected and influential member of the cabinet. That said, it is generally acknowledged that he attends meetings of both parliament and the cabinet only occasionally,” he noted. “In my opinion, sidelining these institutions and instead inviting the country’s distinguished and respected business leaders to speak before a captive audience on such an important issue does not carry the same weight or receive the same recognition as discussing it in the relevant constitutional forums,” Asif stated. Asif added that Naqvi had held powerful positions in Pakistani politics for the past three-and-a-half years and could have initiated a discussion or made progress towards systemic reform during that time. “Nevertheless, better late than never.” Asif also referred to a press conference by ISPR chief Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, who mentioned the 13 points of the National Action Plan. “One of those points — which was the responsibility of our armed forces — is being implemented and fulfilled through the sacrifice of lives. The remaining 12 points fall under the responsibility of the Ministry of Interior, and they have not been implemented,” he noted. “Mr Naqvi should begin reforming the system by implementing the National Action Plan. Let systemic change begin with his own ministry. It is not only our respected business community — the entire nation stands with him.” Various political parties have demanded the creation of more provinces or administrative units to ensure better governance. The MQM-P — an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh. However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move. On the other hand, the PPP and the PTI have long advocated for a South Punjab province . A day prior, Inter-Services Public Relations chief Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry commented on Naqvi’s remarks about the need for new administrative units in Pakistan: “We have been saying this earlier also as a primary stakeholder in security that good governance is essential for the security and stability of Pakistan.” “Now our population is 240-250 million people, and we still have four provinces. We have to see whether this is serving the purpose of good governance. That debate has to be sensibly held by politicians, by those in power, even those who have previously been in power, and those who are responsible to the people of Pakistan,” the DG ISPR said, adding that it had to be done according to the will of the people of Pakistan. Later on Friday, PPP Secretary-General Nayyar Bokhari said that the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) will deliberate on creating new administrative units, which should be created through the mechanism provided in the Constitution rather than by executive order. “The Constitution of Pakistan has clearly laid down the complete procedure. Without a two-thirds majority in the relevant provincial assembly, the National Assembly and the Senate, neither the creation of new provinces nor any alteration in provincial boundaries is possible,” he told Dawn . “New provinces cannot be created through an executive order. They can only be created through a constitutional decision of parliament,” he added. Additional reporting by Ikram Junaidi

PPP, PML-N continue war of words on eve of Muzaffarabad elections. The PPP and the PML-N continued lambasting each other on Saturday, extending their rhetoric from the ongoing elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) to the other party’s previous tenures in power. The PPP and the PML-N — coalition partners in the Centre — have been engaged in a war of words since the PML-N emerged as the winner in the elections in AJK’s Mirpur division. The PPP has accused the PML-N of rigging in Mirpur and demanded re-polling. Political temperatures remain high as the second phase of AJK elections is set to be held tomorrow in nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division. The third phase is scheduled for August 10 in all 12 refugee constituencies and 11 constituencies of Poonch division. In the latest exchange, PML-N senior leader Rana Sanaullah remarked on President Asif Ali Zardari’s role as he responded to PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s allegations of rigging in the 2024 general elections . “If you call the votes secured by the prime minister votes of Forms-47, then on what forms has the president gotten votes on?” Sanaullah said. On Wednesday, Bilawal had taken a direct jibe at Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, saying: “If someone is sitting on the PM’s seat, or someone is sitting on the CM’s position today, even a child knows that it is not because of the people’s votes or your performance but because of Form-47.” Sanaullah, also the prime minister’s aide on political affairs and a federal minister, was addressing a gathering in Jhelum Valley alongside Kashmir Affairs Minister Amir Muqam. Sanaullah further said: “If you say to Mian Nawaz Sharif that he became the prime minister for the first time or every time through rigging, […] then remember, it is also discussed here that someone also became the prime minister for the first time after breaking apart the country.” He was referring to PPP founder Zulfikar Ali Bhutto , who became the president of Pakistan in December 1971 after the secession of Bangladesh (then-East Pakistan) following the 1970 elections . In August 1973, Bhutto took the oath as the prime minister in 1973 under the new Constitution. Sanaullah also took a jibe at Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, whose recent remarks have sparked a fresh debate in political circles on the matter of creating new provinces. Calling Naqvi a “blessed one” of President Zardari, the PML-N leader said the interior minister had “made the [political] journey of 30 years in three-and-a-half years”. “You began from where and have now reached where, and now you realise that this system is completely dysfunctional.” In his speech, Muqam criticised the PPP’s governance in Sindh, saying that no performance of the party could be seen. He also said the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) — a scheme that the PPP often takes credit for launching — was not “anyone’s personal programme but the government’s”. Earlier on Saturday, PPP leader Saeed Ghani alleged that the PML-N had never won a general election without rigging. He further claimed that his party “became a target of rigging” in the 1988 and 1990 elections , which resulted in the PML-N winning. He went on to allege that the PPP was again “controlled and prevented from forming a government in Punjab” in 1993. Ghani alleged that the PPP was restricted to “16-17 seats” in the 1997 general elections , when Nawaz’s PML-N again formed the government. He contended that although the PPP secured power in 2008, the “PML-N was made to win seats, especially in Punjab, through rigging during Musharraf’s tenure”. No matter how many times they say, everyone, even children, know that the PML-N was badly defeated in the elections,” he asserted. The PPP leader alleged that Nawaz, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz “lost their own seats and then blame us”. Ghani made the remarks after explaining the rationale for his party’s stances on new provinces in Sindh and Punjab, stressing that it was based on the wishes of the people. At the outset of his press conference, Ghani also took exception to comments made by “two ministers”, saying it seemed that they “did not know anything about Sindh”. “They are restricted within a circle called Maryam Nawaz. They only see and say what she tells them, shows them and explains to them,” he said in an apparent reference to the Punjab ministers.

Most parts of country brace for heavy rains. LAHORE: The Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) on Saturday forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across parts of Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan until Aug 4. The Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), meanwhile, said river flows, dams and barrages across Punjab were being monitored continuously. It warned that low-level flooding was currently being recorded in the Indus River at Kalabagh and Chashma and that the prevailing weather system was likely to persist until Aug 5. According to the FFD, a well-marked low-pressure system over southeast Raja­s­­than in India, coupled with strong monsoon currents, is expected to trigger a widespread wet spell over central and eastern Punjab as well as parts of Sindh and Balochistan. The system is likely to produce heavy to very heavy rainfall through Aug 4, significantly increasing water flows in the eastern rivers — Sutlej, Ravi and Beas — and their major tributaries. The division said water levels in the River Chenab at Head Marala, Khanki and Qadirabad were likely to rise to the low-to-medium flood category during the forecast period. However, exceptionally high inflows could push the river to a high flood level at Head Marala. Chenab may reach high flood level at Marala; PDMA issues fresh monsoon safety advisory The FFD also warned of possible flash flooding in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams originating in Khyber Pa­­k­­tunkhwa and northern Balochistan, as well as other vulnerable catchment areas. Urban flooding is also feared in several Punjab cities due to the forecast of intense rainfall. The areas at risk include Rawalpindi, Jhelum, Gujranwala, Sargodha, Mandi Bahauddin, Sialkot, Gujrat, Narowal, Lahore, Okara, Sahiwal and Faisalabad. The FFD further said water flows were expected to increase in tributary streams of the River Jhelum, including the Dora, Dota, Dwara, Bhimber and Halsi nullahs. Similar increases are anticipated in the Aik and Palkhu nullahs, which feed the River Chenab, as well as the Bein, Basantar, Deg and Sukki nullahs associated with the River Ravi. Reviewing the current hydrological situation, the FFD said the River Indus was flowing at low flood levels at Kalabagh, Chashma, Guddu and Sukkur. In contrast, the Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum and Sutlej rivers were currently flowing below the low flood level. The division forecast that the Indus at Sukkur would remain in the low flood category at the upstream section over the next 24 hours. It also predicted flash flooding in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams in KP and northern Balo­chistan, and parts of Punjab and Sindh. For the next 24 hours, the FFD forecast widespread rain, wind and thunderstorms, with isolated heavy to very heavy falls over parts of Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan. It also expected scattered rain and thunderstorms, accompanied by isolated heavy falls, over the upper catchments of all major rivers, Islamabad, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and KP. Highest rainfall in Pindi Meanwhile, the PDMA reported widespread rainfall across Punjab during the past 24 hours. Rawalpindi received the highest rainfall at 95 millimetres, followed by Murree (85mm), Jauharabad (56mm), Multan (37mm), Bhakkar (31mm), Narowal and Noorpur Thal (27mm each), Khanewal (21mm), Chakwal (20mm), Gujranwala (12mm), Jhang (10mm) and Sargodha (8mm). The PDMA urged citizens to observe safety precautions during the ongoing wet spell, advising parents to keep children away from rainwater drains, low-lying areas, rivers and canals to avoid accidents. Presidential nod delay hits judiciary appointments. ISLAMABAD: The delay in presidential assent to judicial appointments has begun to affect the functioning of the superior judiciary, with the term of an additional judge of the Sindh High Court (SHC) having already expired and four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court (PHC) facing a similar situation within days, despite recommendations by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) for the continuation of their services. Justice Khalid Hussain Shahani of the SHC was appointed as an additional judge on Jan 29, 2025, for a one-year term. On Jan 22 this year, President Asif Ali Zardari approved a six-month extension in accordance with the JCP’s recommendation, extending his tenure until July 29. Before the expiry of his tenure, the JCP, at its meeting on July 20, recommended another six-month extension and forwarded the recommendation through the constitutional channel to the president, who is the appointing authority. However, the summary has remained pending with the Presidency and no notification has yet been issued. With no formal approval forthcoming, Justice Shahani’s term expired on July 29. Despite this, the SHC included his name in the latest roster of judges constituting benches, anticipating that the notification would be issued in the meantime. SHC judge’s term lapses as four PHC judges face similar uncertainty Sources in the Presidency maintained that an additional judge could not continue to hold office beyond the expiry of his tenure unless the president formally approved the extension and the Law Ministry issued the notification. The sources recalled the case of former Islamabad High Court judge Justice Shaukat Aziz Siddiqui, whose confirmation as an additional judge was rejected by then president Asif Ali Zardari in October 2012 despite the JCP’s recommendation. The matter was later resolved by the Law Ministry, but when it reached the Supreme Court, the apex court observed that, following the 18th and 19th Constitutional Amendments, the president’s role in the appointment of judges had become largely ceremonial and that he was bound to act on the prime minister’s advice. When contacted, SHC Registrar Asif Qureshi said he would examine the matter. A similar situation is emerging in the Peshawar High Court (PHC), where the tenure of four additional judges — Justice Farah Jamshed, Justice Inamullah Khan, Justice Sabitullah Khan and Justice Aurangzeb — is due to expire on Aug 4. The four judges were appointed as additional judges on Feb 4, 2025. When the JCP met on Jan 15 to consider the confirmation of 10 PHC additional judges, it confirmed six as permanent judges while recommending a six-month extension for the remaining four. The president subsequently approved the extension, which is now nearing completion. The JCP has since recommended a further extension for the four judges, but the matter, like that of Justice Shahani, is awaiting presidential approval. The uncertainty comes days after the Presidency also delayed assent to the appointment of additional judges to the Islamabad, Lahore, Sindh and Balochistan high courts, prompting concern within judicial and legal circles. The recommendations, approved by the JCP on July 20 and 21, have yet to be notified, while the government is said to be examining constitutional options should the delay persist. Pakistan Bar Council Vice Chairman Pir Masood Chishti said an additional judge whose notification had not been issued by the president could not continue to perform judicial functions after the expiry of his or her tenure. “Once the president grants approval and the Law Ministry issues the notification, the judges can resume office,” he said. Supreme Court Bar Association Presi­dent Haroon Rashid criticised the continued delay, arguing that the president could not indefinitely withhold confirmation of, or appointments recommended through, the constitutional process. US govt advises Americans to leave Mideast. • US embassies urge citizens to ‘consider departing’ the region • Iran says any country acting as US defensive shield will be engulfed by flames of war • Official insists Tehran planning for worst-case scenarios • 30 commercial vessels redirected by US naval blockade, says Centcom • Tanker struck by ‘unknown projectile’ off Oman; Kuwait destroys hostile drones • Houthis deny plans to impose fees on ships sailing through Red Sea TEHRAN: United States embassies in capitals across the Middle East urged Ame­rican citizens to beware of an “unforeseen escalation” in the regional conflict and asked them to be ready to leave on Saturday as Iran’s military accused the US of “escalating tensions” in the region and warned countries against cooperating with Washington. The messages urged citizens to check flight details and to follow safety advice from local authorities. “Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise caution and heightened vigilance and should be prepared for flight cancellations, periodic airspace closures, and potential travel disruptions,” it said. Americans in Jordan were told not to visit US military bases there, which have recently come under Iranian missile att­ack, and in Israel they were urged to seek the location of the nearest bomb shelter. “The Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or provocations as well as to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted [such as Egypt],” said a post on the US Embassy Jerusalem site. Iran’s warning “The United States is rapidly moving down the path of escalating tensions in the region,” said Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran’s military central command. “Any country serving as a defensive shield for criminal and aggressive America will be engulfed by the flames of war,” he said in a statement read on state television. The remarks came after US President Donald Trump reiterated threats to hit Iran “very hard”. US media reported he was considering renewed heavy attacks as soon as this weekend, including against energy infrastructure targets. This week, Iran and the US resumed overnight exchanges of fire after a days-long lull in fighting although there were no reported strikes overnight Friday to Saturday. Despite having endured “wars, pressure, and relentless hostilities”, Pezeshkian wrote on X, “The future of Iran will be shaped by the people of Iran.” Separately, Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref was quoted by the semi-official Fars news agency as saying that the country was preparing supplies for the next two years, without elaborating on the types of supplies, Al Jazeera reported. The official said maintaining peace among the people would continue to be the main priority and that the government was planning “even for the worst conditions”. Kuwait ‘destroys hostile drones’ On Wednesday a drone struck a US-owned gas vessel moored in an Egyptian port, causing a fire. Egypt is investigating but has not yet accused any group of launching the attack. Meanwhile an “unknown projectile” struck a tanker off the coast of Oman, a British maritime agency said on Saturday, as the United States and Iran vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait’s army also said on Saturday it had detected and destroyed hostile drones in the country’s airspace since dawn, and that what it described as an Iranian attack had targeted several vital facilities. A government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian property belonging to a company on Bubiyan Island were hit, it said, adding that falling shrapnel caused material damage but no casualties. Iran has effectively maintained control over navigation through Hormuz since the outbreak of the war, requiring vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the waterway. Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler said on Friday that traffic through the Hormuz strait has dropped “sharply”. US Central Command (Centcom) said that as part of the naval blockade of Iranian ports, American forces have redirected 30 commercial vessels, boarded two and disabled two others. Meanwhile, a merchant vessel safely passed through the Red Sea under the protection of the Italian frigate Bergamini, the European Union naval mission ASPIDES said on Saturday. ASPIDES, the EU’s defensive maritime security operation in the Red Sea, did not identify the vessel or disclose its flag, ownership or cargo details. Houthis deny plans to impose fees Separately, Yemen’s Houthi-run maritime coordination body denied on Saturday that it planned to impose fees on commercial ships transiting the Bab al-Mandeb strait, saying no such decision had been taken and that passage through the strategic waterway remained free. The Houthi-run Humanitarian Operations Coordination Center (HOCC) said its “safe transit service was a voluntary and cost-free service”. “The HOCC categorically confirms that any individual or entity requesting the payment of money in exchange for transiting the Bab el-Mandeb strait does not represent the Republic of Yemen or HOCC in any capacity whatsoever,” it said in a statement. “The HOCC urges shipping companies not to make any payments or provide any information to unauthorized individuals or entities,” it said. Iranian oil smuggling drops 60pc, claim sources. KARACHI: The influx of smuggled Iranian oil has drastically declined as tankers were hit inside Balo­chistan, causing heavy losses to those involved in this illegal business, according to sources in the oil sector. The oil companies have been demanding that oil smuggling be stopped, but it has continued for years. However, the arrival of Iranian petroleum products increased after the US-Israeli war on Tehran began, pushing crude oil prices above $100 per barrel. “Over the past month and a half, at least six oil tankers coming from Iran were destroyed by terrorists, but the actual number is not known,” said the source familiar with those in the oil business. However, it was not confirmed by other sources. Since the US-Israeli attack on Iran on Feb 28, the entire world was shocked due to due to closure of the Strait of Hormuz , which is the world’s most critical energy transit chokepoint, carrying roughly 20pc of global oil, 20pc of liquefied natural gas (LNG), and about one-third of the world’s fertiliser trade. Influx slows after terrorists destroyed six tankers in 45 days Reserves of petroleum products began to decline in countries like Pakistan, which depend largely on imported fuel. Pakistan faced the same situation, but the country did not experience rationing of oil and gas products. Reserves for 25 days were available, while more ships entered Pakistan during the war. However, the influx of Iranian oil increased significantly. Smuggled petroleum products were available not only in Balochistan but also in Sindh, up to Karachi. Many say that Punjab also benefited from these smuggled oil products, which helped the country avoid rationing of oil products, as seen in India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka in the region. “It is difficult to determine the proportions of previous and current influxes, but smuggling has decreased significantly, by at least 60pc,” the source claimed. In FY26, Pakistan spent a record $16.86bn on the import of petroleum products, which was around 22pc of the country’s total import bill. Notably, despite higher prices, the share of petroleum products in the import bill remained within the average. Each year, Pakistan has to spend 22-25pc of its total imports on oil products. According to the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, the import bill for petroleum products in FY25 was $15.94bn. Pakistan’s illegal trade with Iran is worth more than $2 billion per year, and a number of products, such as edible oil, food products, washing powder, soaps, etc., are readily available in Karachi. It is widely believed in the circles of trade and industry that the smuggling of oil products from Iran was deliberately ignored by the authorities due to the war and to avoid a crisis from a possible shortage of oil supplies across the country. 14 Afghan migrants found dead in desert. • Vehicle broke down in Nimroz; group pressed on toward Iran on foot • Bodies found buried beneath sand HERAT: The bodies of 14 Afghans attempting to reach Iran were found in a scorching desert in southwestern Afghanistan, officials said on Saturday, weeks after their vehicle broke down and they set off by foot. Authorities have been searching for the group since the driver of the vehicle staggered into a village in Nimroz province, parched and exhausted, seeking help. Five bodies were found soon after, but authorities launched a hunt for 14 others who had continued the journey on foot. Nimroz is one of Afghanistan’s hottest and most arid provinces, with temperatures hovering around 45C at this time of year. The 14 bodies were found buried in sand, a source at the Nimroz provincial hospital told AFP on Saturday. Provincial government spokesman Abdul Mutawakil Tawhidi confirmed the grisly desert find on Friday. Iran is a popular destination for Afghan migrants seeking economic opportunity not available at home, but legal avenues for entry are scarce. “These 14 young men are from our village. They had left home 23 days ago, and today we are receiving their bodies,” Abdul Khaleq, a resident of Qolghi in the eastern province of Badghis, told AFP before heading to the cemetery for the burial. Afghan authorities are “firmly continuing their fight against (…) human trafficking,” Interior Ministry spokesman Abdul Mateen Qani said in a statement to national broadcaster RTA . While temperatures in the border areas between Afghanistan and Iran can soar in the summer, they also plummet to dangerous levels in the winter. At least 18 Afghans attempting the perilous crossing into Iran died in the cold last December, including a fifteen-year-old boy. Published in Dawn, August 2nd, 2026

‘US may not have enough forces to defend Israel against Iran’. • Top American commander warns navy is stretched too thin; US has used nearly half of its THAAD interceptors • Pentagon may face choice between US interests and Israel • Missile defences consumed faster than they can be replaced; war tests Washington’s ability to fight on multiple fronts WASHINGTON: A warning from one of America’s top military commanders has exposed a growing dilemma for Washington: The United States may no longer have enough naval forces to simultaneously defend Israel against Iranian missile attacks and protect its own interests across the Middle East. General Alexus Grynkewich, commander of US European Command, has privately informed Pentagon officials that American naval assets are becoming stretched too thin as the conflict with Iran continues, according to reports by The Washington Post and other news outlets. The general reportedly warned that without another US Navy destroyer assigned to the region, commanders could eventually face a difficult choice between protecting American forces and continuing missile-defence operations for Israel. News outlets noted that the significance of the warning lies not only in the shortage itself, but in who delivered it. Grynkewich is not an outside analyst; he is one of the senior officers responsible for managing US military commitments. His message reflects an internal military concern that America’s global commitments are exceeding available resources. Navy destroyers equipped with the Aegis combat system have become a central part of Israel’s missile defence. These ships can track incoming ballistic missiles and launch advanced interceptors such as SM-3 and SM-6 missiles. But these destroyers are also among America’s most valuable global military assets. They are needed in the Pacific to deter China, in Europe to reassure Nato allies, and in the Middle East to protect American bases and shipping routes. His warning highlights a difficult military calculation: Every ship sent to defend Israel is a ship unavailable for another potential crisis. The warning comes amid reports that the United States has carried a substantial share of the burden in defending Israel from Iranian missile attacks. Pentagon assessments cited by The Washington Post indicate US forces fired more than 200 THAAD interceptors during the Iran conflict — roughly half the Pentagon’s reported inventory — along with over 100 interceptors launched from Navy ships. Israel also used its own Arrow and David’s Sling systems but relied heavily on American support during the most intense missile exchanges. The issue is not simply the number of missiles fired. Advanced interceptors are expensive, complex weapons that take years to manufacture and replace. Recent assessments have warned that prolonged combat could place pressure on US stockpiles of critical air-defence weapons. For decades, American military strategy has rested on the belief that Washington can respond to multiple crises simultaneously. The United States maintains alliances in Europe, commitments in the Middle East, and a growing military focus on the Indo-Pacific. The warning from US European Command suggests that this assumption is being tested. The problem facing Pentagon planners is not whether the United States has the strongest military in the world — it does. The problem is whether even the strongest military has enough ships, missiles, and industrial capacity to sustain simultaneous commitments. A conflict with Iran may therefore be revealing a broader vulnerability: America’s military power is vast, but not unlimited. According to an analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies cited by CNN , the military has used a significant portion of its advanced missile inventory in recent weeks of fighting. The assessment estimates that American forces have consumed about 45pc of their Precision Strike Missiles, at least half of their THAAD interceptors, and around 50pc of their Patriot interceptors. The analysis also indicates the US has used roughly 30pc of its Tomahawk cruise missiles, over 20pc of its Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles, and around 20pc of its SM-3 and SM-6 interceptors. Either way, the message from inside the Pentagon is clear: Modern warfare is consuming advanced weapons faster than they can be replaced, and even the US military must make choices when several crises demand the same resources. Urban flooding. THE warning from the disaster management and weather authorities that a new monsoon spell could trigger urban flooding in major cities across Punjab and Sindh is yet another reminder of how poorly prepared our cities are for heavy rainfall. Cities from Rawalpindi, Lahore and Multan in Punjab, to Hyderabad, Umerkot and Tando Allahyar in Sindh, have been flagged for urban flooding. This is not unusual during the monsoons. However, what makes this year’s warning worth pausing on is the Met Office’s forecast of below normal rainfall this year. Still, less rainfall will not eliminate the risk of flooded cities if a burst of rain arrives faster than the ground and drains can carry it away. This says more about the state of our cities than about the weather. The problem of urban flooding in Pakistan is no longer limited to low-lying neighbourhoods. It has become a structural feature of how the country has grown and urban centres have developed. Unplanned construction has taken place over drainage channels and wetlands that once absorbed rain. Waterways have been encroached upon, storm-water systems are built for outdated rainfall patterns, and drains are choked with solid waste that no longer has any place to go. The response is reactive across the provinces. Drains are cleared only when the rain starts to fall; pumps arrive after roads are under water; and warnings are issued, repeated, then forgotten until the next spell. This is crisis management dressed up as preparedness. Most Pakistani cities have no comprehensive flood-risk maps, no functioning drainage master plans, and no clear chain of command for who acts first as the water rises. Drainage, roads, water supply and disaster response sit in separate departments that rarely coordinate before a flood and mostly trade blame after one. Climate change has broken the old planning assumptions. Cities now need infrastructure built for short, intense downpours capable of overwhelming drains within minutes, not the gradual rainfall patterns those systems were designed around decades ago. Every new road, housing scheme or commercial project should be assessed for how it disrupts the natural water flow before approval, not after the damage becomes visible. Existing drains need redesigning and expanding to match current rainfall intensity, rather than being patched up just before the monsoon. Pakistan cannot control how much rain falls. But it can control the extent to which the rain turns into a disaster. The recent warning is not a new problem; each year, governments assure the public that they are ready for the rains. Unfortunately, the very first intense downpour exposes their claims. What the country needs is sustained investment in drainage infrastructure and local governments to maintain it between the monsoons, not just during the rainy season.
